ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a broken-line graph of inductor coil current i varying with time t, with the vertical axis as i(A) and the horizontal axis as t(s). Reading from the graph: during 0–2 s, the current linearly increases from 0 A to 4 A; during 2–4 s, the current remains unchanged at 4 A; during 4–6 s, the current linearly increases from 4 A to 6 A; during 6–8 s, the current linearly decreases from 6 A to 0 A. Reasoning: The magnitude of the self-induced electromotive force is proportional to the absolute value of the current rate of change, namely |E| = L|Δi/Δt|. Calculate the slope of each segment separately: 0–2 s, Δi/Δt = (4−0)/2 = 2 A/s; 2–4 s, Δi/Δt = 0 A/s; 4–6 s, Δi/Δt = (6−4)/2 = 1 A/s; 6–8 s, Δi/Δt = (0−6)/2 = −3 A/s, whose absolute value is 3 A/s. The maximum absolute rate of change occurs during 6–8 s, so the self-induced electromotive force is maximum during 6–8 s.
